edits.old: Management, in one line Management is not the fork this question tests, so in one sentence: replace what is missing and cover what the defect exposes — immunoglobulin replacement for any low-IgG defect plus antibiotic prophylaxis (in-context; TMP-SMX as the agent is memory-sourced ⚠︎), no live vaccines ⚠︎, washed/IgA-depleted products instead of IVIG in selective IgA deficiency ⚠︎, and allogeneic HSCT as the only cure for CD40L deficiency ⚠︎.
edits.new: Long-term treatment matched to the defect Common variable immunodeficiency and XLA — lifelong immunoglobulin replacement (IV or subcutaneous) and prompt antibiotics for each infection; in CVID it cuts infections but not the autoimmune and lymphoma risk, so both stay on the follow-up list · Hyper-IgM syndrome (CD40 ligand deficiency) — immunoglobulin replacement plus trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole against Pneumocystis; hematopoietic stem cell transplant is the only cure · Selective IgA deficiency — no immunoglobulin replacement; washed or IgA-deficient blood products if transfused · SCID and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome — hematopoietic stem cell transplant, which fixes the missing lymphocyte line; it is not used for CVID · Complete (athymic) DiGeorge syndrome — cultured thymus tissue transplant; the defect is the thymus, not the marrow · Chronic granulomatous disease — interferon gamma plus trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and itraconazole prophylaxis · Antiviral and antifungal prophylaxis — belongs to impaired cellular immunity (SCID, T-cell defects, CGD), not to a pure antibody defect with bacterial and Giardia infections · Live vaccines — withheld in major antibody defects and in T-cell or combined defects
edits.why: Q6 tests long-term management, so the block that said management is not tested is replaced by a treatment-to-defect map covering the key (IVIG for CVID) and every distractor (HSCT for SCID, thymus transplant for DiGeorge, interferon gamma for CGD, antiviral/antifungal prophylaxis for cellular defects); unneeded flags on standard facts removed.
